1.caption: Members gather in the House of Representatives chamber; painted by Samuel F. B. Morse, 1822.
1.basis: Painted by Samuel F. B. Morse in 1822 to 1823 (he died in 1872), so copyright expired long ago; the National Gallery of Art released its photograph as CC0 under its open access policy.

2.caption: The Constitution's signed fourth page, 1787; its Article VI declares it the supreme law.
2.basis: The Constitution was written by the Constitutional Convention in 1787, so any copyright expired long ago; the scan was made by the U.S. National Archives, a federal agency (record 1667751).

3.caption: Assembly Room, Independence Hall, Philadelphia, where the Constitution was written and signed in 1787.
3.basis: Photograph by National Park Service staff, taken 21 December 2015 and published in the agency's NPGallery as public domain, so it is a work of the U.S. federal government.

4.caption: "We the People", the first words of the Constitution, written in 1787.
4.basis: Part of the Constitution written by the Constitutional Convention in 1787, so any copyright expired long ago; scanned by the U.S. National Archives, a federal agency (record 1667751).

5.caption: Alice Paul unfurls a banner celebrating ratification of the 19th Amendment, August 1920.
5.credit: National Photo Company, Library of Congress
5.basis: Photograph by the National Photo Company, Washington, made in August 1920 and published in The Suffragist in September 1920, so its U.S. copyright has expired (published before 1930).

6.caption: The Bill of Rights: amendments Congress proposed in 1789; ten were ratified in 1791.
6.basis: The joint resolution of the First Congress of 1789, a federal document whose copyright, if any, expired long ago; scanned by the U.S. National Archives, a federal agency (record 1408042).

8.caption: Thomas Jefferson's handwritten rough draft of the Declaration of Independence, June 1776.
8.basis: Written by Thomas Jefferson in June 1776 (he died in 1826), so any copyright expired long ago; the scan comes from the Library of Congress, which states no known restriction on use.

9.caption: John Trumbull's painting in the U.S. Capitol: the drafting committee presents the Declaration, 1776.
9.basis: Painted by John Trumbull (died 1843) in 1817-1818 for the U.S. Capitol and shown publicly from 1818, so its U.S. copyright expired long ago (before 1930).

10.caption: The Liberty Bell, with Independence Hall behind, where the Declaration and Constitution were signed.
10.basis: Photographed on 12 July 2013 by the National Park Service (credit 'NPS photo', published by NPS on NPGallery as 'Public domain: Full Granting Rights'), so it is a U.S. federal government work.

11.caption: The Declaration of Independence, printed from William J. Stone's 1823 copperplate engraving.
11.basis: Text adopted by the Continental Congress in 1776 and engraved on copper by William J. Stone (died 1865) in 1823, with this state printed about 1833; its copyright expired (published before 1930).

12.caption: Entrance of the New York Stock Exchange on Wall Street, with a U.S. flag.
12.basis: Photographed on 21 September 2012 by Wikimedia Commons user Balon Greyjoy, who published his own photo under CC0 (public domain dedication by the author).

13.caption: The U.S. Supreme Court building; 'Equal Justice Under Law' is carved above the columns.
13.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
13.basis: Photographed by Carol M. Highsmith between 1980 and 2006; she dedicated her archive at the Library of Congress to the public domain (LCCN 2011631106).

14.caption: The Federalist (the Federalist Papers): title page of the 1802 New York edition.
14.basis: Book by Hamilton, Madison and Jay (writing as Publius), printed by George F. Hopkins in New York in 1802; its copyright expired (published before 1930).

15.caption: The Capitol, where Congress meets; behind it, the Supreme Court (left) and Library of Congress.
15.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
15.basis: Photographed by Carol M. Highsmith on 30 April 2007; she dedicated her archive at the Library of Congress to the public domain (LCCN 2010630477).

16.caption: Chief Justice Stone swears in President Truman as House Speaker Rayburn looks on, 1945.
16.basis: Photograph by Abbie Rowe, a National Park Service staff photographer, taken 12 April 1945 as part of his job; a U.S. federal government work (Truman Library accession 73-1909, rights: Public Domain).

17.caption: The White House, home and workplace of the President, seen from the air in 2007.
17.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
17.basis: Photo by Carol M. Highsmith, 30 April 2007, from the archive she gave to the Library of Congress and dedicated to the public domain (LC-DIG-highsm-04919; Library of Congress: no known restrictions on publication).

18.caption: The dome of the U.S. Capitol, where Congress meets.
18.basis: Official photograph by staff of the Architect of the Capitol, a federal agency, taken 26 January 2022; a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov-Congress-AOC).

19.caption: The U.S. Capitol, west front: Senate wing at left, House wing at right.
19.basis: Photograph by the Architect of the Capitol, a federal agency, 1997; a U.S. federal government work. The Wikimedia Commons file (3000 x 1556) is a cropped version of the original (3000 x 2400) published on aoc.gov, archived at https://web.archive.org/web/20070228191918/http://www.aoc.gov/cc/photo-gallery/upload/72350_hr_1997.jpg

20.caption: The 1941 joint resolution of Congress declaring war on Japan.
20.basis: Official record of the U.S. Congress dated 8 December 1941, scanned by the National Archives (catalog id 299850); a U.S. federal government work.

21.caption: The U.S. Senate Chamber, with a desk for each senator, in a 1921 encyclopedia.
21.basis: Photograph by Harris & Ewing printed in Collier's New Encyclopedia, volume 10, published in the United States in 1921; published before 1930, so the copyright has expired.

22.caption: The Senate wing of the U.S. Capitol, where senators serve six-year terms.
22.basis: Official photograph by staff of the Architect of the Capitol, a federal agency, taken 26 January 2022; a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov-Congress-AOC).

23.caption: The Russell Senate Office Building, where many senators have their offices.
23.basis: Official photograph by staff of the Architect of the Capitol, a federal agency, taken 16 January 2014; a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov-Congress-AOC).

24.caption: The House of Representatives in session, from a 1921 encyclopedia.
24.basis: Photograph by the Keystone View Company printed in Collier's New Encyclopedia, volume 10, published in the United States in 1921; published before 1930, so the copyright has expired.

25.caption: The House of Representatives, painted by Samuel F. B. Morse in 1822.
25.basis: Painting of 1822 by Samuel F. B. Morse (died 1872), long out of copyright; the National Gallery of Art released its photograph as CC0 under its open access policy.

26.caption: Stump Speaking, painted by George Caleb Bingham in 1853-54: a candidate addresses voters.
26.basis: Painted in 1853-54 by George Caleb Bingham (died 1879), so U.S. copyright expired long ago; the file is a faithful photo of the flat painting (Commons tag PD-Art, PD-old-auto-expired).

27.caption: The Senate chamber in the U.S. Capitol, photographed about 1873.
27.basis: Glass negative made between 1860 and 1880 by the Brady-Handy studio, held by the Library of Congress (cwpbh.03299), which states no known restrictions; any copyright expired long ago.

28.caption: The Assembly Room of Independence Hall, where the Constitution was debated in 1787.
28.basis: National Park Service staff photo taken 21 December 2015 and published on NPGallery as 'NPS Photo, Public domain: Full Granting Rights'; a work of the U.S. federal government.

29.caption: The east front of the U.S. Capitol at sunrise, with the House wing nearest.
29.basis: Official photo by the Architect of the Capitol, a federal agency, taken 31 January 2022; a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov-Congress-AOC).

30.caption: Members applaud two astronauts in the House chamber, 1965; the Speaker's rostrum is at center.
30.basis: NASA photograph S65-44234 from the Johnson Space Center, dated 14 September 1965; a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov-NASA).

31.caption: The Senate wing of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.
31.basis: Official photo by the Architect of the Capitol, a federal agency, taken 26 January 2022; a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov-Congress-AOC).

32.caption: 1913 government notice that the Seventeenth Amendment, on electing senators, was ratified.
32.basis: Printed notice issued by the U.S. Department of State on 31 May 1913, held by the National Archives (catalog ID 28264994); a federal government work that was also published before 1930.

33.caption: U.S. Geological Survey map of congressional districts for the 91st Congress (1969-1971); lines differ today.
33.basis: Map from The National Atlas of the United States, published by the U.S. Geological Survey in 1970 from Census Bureau data; a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov).

34.caption: Canvassing for a Vote, by George Caleb Bingham, 1852: a candidate asks citizens for votes.
34.basis: Painted in 1852 by George Caleb Bingham (died 1879), so U.S. copyright expired long ago; the file is a faithful photo of the flat painting in the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art (Commons tag PD-Art, PD-old-100).

35.caption: A census taker interviews a farmer in a field for the 1940 census.
35.basis: Photograph made by the U.S. Bureau of the Census for the 1940 census, confirmed by the Library of Congress record of the same picture; a work of the U.S. federal government.

36.caption: John F. Kennedy's inauguration at the U.S. Capitol, 1961, the start of a four-year term.
36.basis: Photograph by Abbie Rowe, a National Park Service photographer, taken on duty on 20 January 1961 (National Archives 194170); a U.S. federal government work.

37.caption: The joint resolution of Congress that proposed the 22nd Amendment, 1947.
37.basis: An official document of the U.S. Congress (H.J. Res. 27, 80th Congress, 1947) photographed by the National Archives; a U.S. federal government work.

38.caption: The White House, home and office of the President, north front, April 2020.
38.basis: Official White House photo by staff photographer Andrea Hanks, 3 April 2020, made as part of the job; a U.S. federal government work.

39.caption: The Eisenhower Executive Office Building, where the Vice President has a ceremonial office.
39.basis: Photographed on 26 March 2015 by Wikimedia Commons user Daderot, who published it as his own work under the CC0 public domain dedication.

40.caption: Vice President Harry Truman takes the oath as President after Roosevelt's death, April 12, 1945.
40.basis: Photograph by Abbie Rowe, a National Park Service photographer, taken on duty on 12 April 1945 (Truman Library 73-1909); a U.S. federal government work.

41.caption: President Carter with Egypt's Sadat and Israel's Begin after signing the Camp David Accords, 1978.
41.basis: Taken by the Carter White House staff photographers on 17 September 1978 (National Archives 181393, Carter Library); a U.S. federal government work.

42.caption: President Lincoln meets General McClellan and Union officers at Antietam, Maryland, October 1862.
42.basis: Photograph by Alexander Gardner (died 1882), made on 3 October 1862, from the Library of Congress Civil War negatives (LC-DIG-cwpb-04352); copyright expired long ago.

43.caption: President Eisenhower signs the Civil Rights Act of 1960 at the White House.
43.basis: Taken by the National Park Service, National Capital Parks, Office of Public Information on 6 May 1960 (National Archives 7865626, Eisenhower Library); a U.S. federal government work.

44.caption: President Reagan signs his veto of a defense bill in the Oval Office, 1988.
44.basis: Taken by the Reagan White House Photographic Office on 3 August 1988 (National Archives 75856223, Reagan Library); a U.S. federal government work.

45.caption: President Nixon with Warren Burger, his nominee for Chief Justice, May 21, 1969.
45.basis: Taken by the Nixon White House Photo Office on 21 May 1969 (National Archives 66394147, Nixon Library); a U.S. federal government work.

46.caption: The Treasury Department, one of the federal executive departments, in Washington, D.C.
46.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
46.basis: Photograph by Carol M. Highsmith, made between 1980 and 2006, who dedicated her Library of Congress archive to the public domain.

47.caption: President Warren Harding, at left, meets with his Cabinet at the White House, 1921.
47.basis: News photograph by Harris & Ewing, 1921, given to the Library of Congress in 1955 (item 2016859363); made before 1930 and the Library lists no known restrictions.

48.caption: President Woodrow Wilson, left, with his Cabinet in the White House Cabinet Room, June 1916.
48.basis: Harris & Ewing studio photograph made in June 1916 (pre-1930, copyright expired); the studio gave its collection to the Library of Congress in 1955 and the Library lists no known restrictions on publication.

49.caption: Massachusetts electors signed this envelope holding their votes for president, December 1860.
49.basis: Scan made in 2019 by U.S. National Archives staff (a federal work) of an 1860 government record whose own copyright, if any, expired long ago.

50.caption: A federal courthouse: the United States Courthouse in Toledo, Ohio, built 1929 to 1932.
50.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
50.basis: Photographed in 2007 by Carol M. Highsmith, who gave her archive to the Library of Congress and dedicated her rights to the public domain.

51.caption: Words from Marbury v. Madison, 1803, carved on a wall in the Supreme Court Building.
51.basis: Photographed in 2008 by Wikimedia user NuclearWarfare, who released all rights to the public domain; the carved words come from an 1803 Supreme Court opinion.

52.caption: The front of the Supreme Court Building in Washington, D.C.
52.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
52.basis: Photograph by Carol M. Highsmith, taken between 1980 and 2006; she gave her archive to the Library of Congress and dedicated her rights to the public domain.

53.caption: The Supreme Court courtroom, with nine chairs behind the bench for the nine justices.
53.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
53.basis: Photograph by Carol M. Highsmith, taken between 1980 and 2006; she gave her archive to the Library of Congress and dedicated her rights to the public domain.

54.caption: The nine Supreme Court justices under Chief Justice Taft, late 1920s. Five sit in front.
54.basis: Harris & Ewing studio portrait of the Taft Court, made between 1925 and early 1930 (copyright expired); the studio gave its collection to the Library of Congress in 1955, which lists no known restrictions.

55.caption: Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. at his desk around 1924. He served until age 90.
55.credit: National Photo Company, Library of Congress
55.basis: National Photo Company news photograph made about 1924 (pre-1930, copyright expired); the Library of Congress, which holds the collection, lists no known restrictions on publication.

56.caption: The words Equal Justice Under Law above the columns of the Supreme Court Building.
56.basis: Own photograph by Wikimedia user Quercusvirginiana, taken in 2019 and released by the author under CC0.

57.caption: The U.S. Supreme Court Building in Washington, D.C.
57.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
57.basis: Photograph by Carol M. Highsmith (between 1980 and 2006), who gave her archive to the public through the Library of Congress; loc.gov item 2011631106 says no known restrictions on publication.

58.caption: Newly struck American Eagle gold coins at the West Point Mint, 2011.
58.basis: Frame from the U.S. Mint's own 2011 production footage, a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov-Treasury).

59.caption: Schoolchildren at their desks in a rural school, San Augustine County, Texas, April 1943.
59.basis: Taken in April 1943 by John Vachon as a federal employee of the Office of War Information, so it is a U.S. government work (PD-USGov-FSA).

60.caption: The Bill of Rights, 1789. Its last article became the 10th Amendment.
60.basis: A 1789 resolution of the U.S. Congress, scanned by the National Archives (NARA id 1408042): a federal government document and long out of copyright.

61.caption: The Illinois State Capitol in Springfield. Every state has its own governor.
61.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
61.basis: Photograph by Carol M. Highsmith (between 1980 and 2006), who gave her archive to the public through the Library of Congress; loc.gov item 2011633217 says no known restrictions on publication.

62.caption: The 50 states and their capitals on a 2003 U.S. Geological Survey map.
62.basis: Map made in 2003 by the U.S. Geological Survey, Department of the Interior, for the National Atlas: a work of the U.S. federal government (PD-USGov-Interior).

63.caption: Women vote at a polling place, probably in New York City, about 1917.
63.credit: National Photo Company Collection, Library of Congress
63.basis: News photograph of about 1917 from the National Photo Company, issued with a printed news caption, so published before 1930 and out of copyright; loc.gov item 97510725 says no known restrictions.

64.caption: The jury box in the Webster County Courthouse, Red Cloud, Nebraska.
64.basis: Own photograph by Wikimedia Commons user Ammodramus, taken on 30 April 2013 and released by the author under CC0 (public domain dedication).

65.caption: A man stands to speak at a town meeting in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, 1947.
65.credit: Ed Westcott, U.S. Department of Energy
65.basis: Taken in 1947 by Ed Westcott, the government photographer at Oak Ridge, as a federal employee, and published by the U.S. Department of Energy as a government work (PD-USGov-DOE).

66.caption: The U.S. flag above Joshua trees, Joshua Tree National Park, California.
66.basis: National Park Service photograph (NPS/Bill Bjornstad, 28 June 2023) published by Joshua Tree National Park as a U.S. government work (PD-USGov-NPS).

67.caption: People raise their right hands for the Oath of Allegiance, Valley Forge, 2024.
67.basis: National Park Service photograph taken on 28 October 2024 at Valley Forge National Historical Park and published in the NPS gallery as public domain (PD-USGov-NPS).

68.caption: Immigrants in an "Americanization" class, about 1920. These classes taught English and civics.
68.credit: National Photo Company, Library of Congress
68.basis: Photograph by the National Photo Company, dated about 1920 by the Library of Congress (https://www.loc.gov/item/2016852098/), which lists no known restrictions on publication; published before 1930, so its copyright has expired.

69.caption: A woman drops her ballot into a glass ballot box, about 1917.
69.credit: National Photo Company Collection, Library of Congress
69.basis: News agency print in the National Photo Company Collection, dated about 1917 by the Library of Congress and carrying a press caption, so its U.S. copyright has expired (published before 1930); the Library lists no known restrictions on publication.

70.caption: A woman takes the oath to join the Women's Army Corps, London, 1944.
70.basis: Official U.S. Army Signal Corps photograph number SC 191946, taken on duty in London on 24 July 1944, so it is a work of the U.S. federal government (Commons tag PD-USGov-Military-Army).

71.caption: Congress's 1909 joint resolution proposing the Sixteenth Amendment on income taxes, ratified in 1913.
71.basis: Enrolled joint resolution of the U.S. Congress from 1909, a federal government document scanned by the National Archives (NAID 1408918, use unrestricted), and also published before 1930.

72.caption: Blindfolded Secretary of War Newton Baker draws a draft lottery number, Washington, June 1918.
72.basis: News photograph by International Film Service, made and printed in newspapers in June 1918, so its U.S. copyright has expired (published before 1930); held by the National Archives (NAID 533713, https://catalog.archives.gov/id/533713) with use marked Unrestricted.

73.caption: Robert Weir's 1843 painting: the Pilgrims pray before leaving Holland for America, 1620.
73.basis: Painting by Robert W. Weir dated 1843 (copyright long expired), photographed by the Architect of the Capitol, a federal office (Commons tag PD-USGov-Congress-AOC).

74.caption: Cliff Palace, Mesa Verde, Colorado, built by Ancestral Pueblo people between about 1190 and 1260.
74.basis: Photographed in 2016 by Warren LeMay (Flickr user w_lemay), who released it as CC0; the Commons Flickr review confirmed the CC0 licence.

75.caption: Olaudah Equiano's autobiography, 1794 edition; he wrote of being taken from Africa and enslaved.
75.basis: Engraved portrait and title page printed in Norwich, England, in 1794, so copyright expired long ago; Library of Congress copy photo, no known restrictions on publication.

76.caption: Washington crossing the Delaware in 1776, during the Revolutionary War; painted by Emanuel Leutze, 1851.
76.basis: Painted by Emanuel Leutze (died 1868) and shown in New York in 1851, so copyright has expired; faithful photo of the painting in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

77.caption: English teapot, made about 1766-1770, painted with the words No Stamp Act.
77.basis: Photo taken in 2011 by Commons user Daderot, who released it into the public domain (PD-self); the teapot itself dates from 1766-1770.

78.caption: Thomas Jefferson, painted by Rembrandt Peale in 1800.
78.basis: Painted by Rembrandt Peale (died 1860) in 1800, so copyright expired long ago; faithful reproduction of the painting in the White House collection.

79.caption: First printing of the Declaration of Independence, headed In Congress, July 4, 1776.
79.basis: Printed by John Dunlap in Philadelphia in July 1776 by order of the Continental Congress, so copyright expired long ago; scan from the U.S. National Archives (NARA 301682).

80.caption: British surrender at Yorktown in 1781, painted by John Trumbull.
80.basis: Painted by John Trumbull (died 1843) in 1820 for the U.S. Capitol and hung in the Rotunda in 1826, so copyright has expired; photo from the Architect of the Capitol.

81.caption: School map from 1919: the thirteen colonies line the Atlantic coast north of Florida.
81.basis: Published in Chicago in 1919 by the McConnell Map Company, so U.S. copyright has expired (before 1930); scan from the Library of Congress.

82.caption: First page of the U.S. Constitution, written in 1787.
82.basis: Handwritten in 1787 for the Constitutional Convention, so any copyright expired long ago; scan from the U.S. National Archives, a federal agency.

83.caption: Alexander Hamilton, painted by John Trumbull about 1805.
83.basis: Painted by John Trumbull (died 1843) about 1805, so copyright expired long ago; faithful reproduction of the painting in the White House collection.

84.caption: Title page of The Federalist, on the new Constitution, by Publius, 1802 edition.
84.basis: Printed in New York by George F. Hopkins in 1802, so copyright expired long ago; plain scan of the printed page.

85.caption: Benjamin Franklin about 1785, when he was U.S. diplomat in France; by Joseph Duplessis.
85.basis: Painted by Joseph Siffred Duplessis (died 1802) about 1785, so copyright expired long ago; reproduction from the National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian, which also marks it CC0.

86.caption: General Washington resigns his army commission to Congress in 1783; painting by John Trumbull.
86.basis: Painted by John Trumbull (died 1843) for the U.S. Capitol and placed in the Rotunda in 1824, so copyright expired long ago; the photo comes from the Architect of the Capitol, a federal office.

87.caption: Thomas Jefferson, painted by Rembrandt Peale in 1800.
87.basis: Painted by Rembrandt Peale (died 1860) in 1800, so copyright has expired in the United States; this is a faithful photo of that flat painting, which hangs in the White House collection.

88.caption: James Madison, painted by John Vanderlyn in 1816.
88.basis: Painted by John Vanderlyn (died 1852) in 1816, so copyright has expired in the United States; this is a faithful photo of that flat painting in the White House collection.

89.caption: Alexander Hamilton, painted by John Trumbull about 1805.
89.basis: Painted by John Trumbull (died 1843) about 1805, so copyright has expired in the United States; this is a faithful photo of that flat painting in the White House collection.

90.caption: 1912 government map showing the Louisiana Purchase, the land bought from France in 1803.
90.basis: Map No. 4 from a 1912 booklet by Frank Bond of the U.S. General Land Office, published by the Government Printing Office: a federal work, and also published before 1930.

91.caption: USS Constitution, a Navy ship that fought in the War of 1812, sailing in 2012.
91.basis: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist Seaman Michael Achterling, taken on duty on 19 August 2012 (photo ID 120819-N-BJ178-989), so it is a work of the federal government.

92.caption: A Union officer faces captured Confederate soldiers; painted by Winslow Homer in 1866.
92.credit: Winslow Homer, Metropolitan Museum of Art
92.basis: Painted by Winslow Homer (died 1910) in 1866, so copyright has expired in the United States; the Metropolitan Museum of Art, which owns it, lists the work as public domain.

93.caption: General Lee surrenders to General Grant at Appomattox, 1865; painting by Alonzo Chappel.
93.basis: Painted by Alonzo Chappel about 1870, so copyright has expired; the Smithsonian American Art Museum released this image as CC0 in its Open Access collection.

94.caption: Abraham Lincoln, photographed by Alexander Gardner on November 8, 1863.
94.basis: Photograph taken by Alexander Gardner (died 1882) on 8 November 1863 and published in the 19th century, so its U.S. copyright expired long ago.

95.caption: First page of the Emancipation Proclamation, January 1, 1863, held by the National Archives.
95.basis: Presidential proclamation issued by Abraham Lincoln on January 1, 1863, a U.S. government document scanned by the National Archives (PD-USGov) and far older than 1930.

96.caption: Civil War Union soldiers: Company E, 4th U.S. Colored Infantry, Fort Lincoln, Washington, D.C.
96.basis: Photograph by William Morris Smith made between 1863 and 1866 and sold as a print in the 1800s (listed in an 1890 catalogue), so its U.S. copyright has expired.

97.caption: First page of the 14th Amendment, as passed by Congress in 1866.
97.basis: Joint resolution of Congress from 1866, a federal government document scanned and published by the National Archives (PD-USGov), and also older than 1930.

98.caption: "The First Vote": Black men voting during Reconstruction, after the Civil War.
98.credit: A. R. Waud, Library of Congress
98.basis: Wood engraving by Alfred R. Waud (died 1891), published on the cover of Harper's Weekly on November 16, 1867, so its U.S. copyright has expired.

99.caption: Elizabeth Cady Stanton (seated) and Susan B. Anthony (standing), photographed between 1880 and 1902.
99.basis: Mounted studio photograph made between 1880 and 1902 by a photographer the Library of Congress does not name; over 120 years old, no known restrictions, copyright expired.

100.caption: Japan signs the surrender on USS Missouri, September 2, 1945, ending World War II.
100.basis: Taken on duty by U.S. Army Signal Corps photographer Lt. Stephen E. Korpanty on September 2, 1945 (photo SC 213700, National Archives), so it is a federal government work.

101.caption: President Wilson asks Congress to declare war on Germany, April 2, 1917.
101.basis: Colour halftone print 'For the freedom of the world', maker not named, copyright registered 21 December 1918 (Library of Congress 2002716887), so published before 1930 and expired.

102.caption: Alice Paul unfurls the ratification banner after Tennessee approved the 19th Amendment, August 1920.
102.credit: National Photo Company, Library of Congress
102.basis: Photograph by National Photo Co., Washington, dated 18 August 1920 and published in The Suffragist in September 1920 (Library of Congress mnwp.160068), so published before 1930 and expired.

103.caption: People wait for relief checks during the Great Depression, Calipatria, California, 1937.
103.basis: Photograph by Dorothea Lange made in March 1937 as a federal employee of the Resettlement Administration, later the Farm Security Administration (Library of Congress fsa.8b31768), so a U.S. government work.

104.caption: The New York Stock Exchange on Wall Street, where stock prices crashed in 1929.
104.basis: Own photograph by Commons user Balon Greyjoy, taken 21 September 2012 and released by the author under the CC0 public domain dedication.

105.caption: President Franklin D. Roosevelt signs the declaration of war against Japan, December 8, 1941.
105.basis: Photograph by Abbie Rowe, National Park Service photographer, 8 December 1941 (National Archives 520053, Record Group 79, 79-AR-82), so a U.S. government work.

106.caption: The USS Arizona Memorial at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, above the sunken battleship.
106.basis: U.S. Navy photograph by Photographer's Mate Jayme Pastoric, 23 May 2002 (Navy ID 020523-N-9769P-057), made on duty, so a U.S. government work.

107.caption: General Eisenhower talks with American paratroopers in England, June 5, 1944, before D-Day.
107.basis: U.S. Army Signal Corps photograph taken 5 June 1944 (Library of Congress cph.3a26521, noted there as 'U.S. Army photograph', No. SC 194399), so a U.S. government work.

108.caption: Soviet leader Gorbachev and President Reagan sign a nuclear arms treaty, Washington, 1987.
108.basis: White House Photographic Office photograph, 8 December 1987 (Reagan Library C44071-15A, National Archives 198588), made by federal staff, so a U.S. government work.

109.caption: Workers put up a fallout shelter sign at a Boston school, December 1962.
109.basis: Photograph from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District, 3 December 1962 (National Archives Record Group 77, Construction Project Photographs), so a U.S. government work.

110.caption: South Korean and U.S. soldiers post a sign at the 38th parallel, Korea, 1950.
110.basis: U.S. Army Signal Corps photo SC 350355, made in 1950 by an Army photographer on duty, so it is a federal work in the public domain (PD-USGov-Military).

111.caption: U.S. Army soldiers and helicopters in South Vietnam, May 1966.
111.basis: Taken on 16 May 1966 by U.S. Army photographer SFC James K. F. Dung on duty (National Archives record 530610, local id 111-C-CC34613), so it is a federal work in the public domain.

112.caption: Civil rights leaders and marchers at the March on Washington, August 28, 1963.
112.basis: Taken on 28 August 1963 by Rowland Scherman on assignment as photographer for the U.S. Information Agency; held in the agency's records at the National Archives (record 542010) with use Unrestricted, a federal work in the public domain.

113.caption: Martin Luther King, Jr. at the March on Washington, August 28, 1963.
113.basis: Taken on 28 August 1963 by Rowland Scherman on assignment for the U.S. Information Agency (National Archives record 542015, use Unrestricted), a federal work in the public domain; the restorer released the clean-up as CC0.

114.caption: U.S. Air Force jets fly over burning oil wells in Kuwait, 1991.
114.basis: U.S. Air Force photo from 1991, published on af.mil and made by Air Force personnel on duty, so it is a federal work in the public domain (PD-USGov-Military-Air Force).

115.caption: The Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, with a flag unfurled in remembrance, September 11, 2014.
115.basis: Department of Defense photo by Army Staff Sgt. Sean K. Harp, taken on duty on 11 September 2014 (VIRIN 140911-D-HU462-038), so it is a federal work in the public domain.

116.caption: U.S. soldiers board a Chinook helicopter in Afghanistan, September 2003.
116.basis: U.S. Army photo by Staff Sgt. Kyle Davis, taken on duty in Afghanistan on 4 September 2003, so it is a federal work in the public domain.

117.caption: Taos Pueblo, New Mexico, home of the Taos Pueblo people, photographed in 1941.
117.basis: Taken in 1941 by Ansel Adams under a National Park Service commission for the Department of the Interior mural project; National Archives record 519984 lists use as Unrestricted and the Archives states this series is in the public domain.

118.caption: Astronaut Buzz Aldrin salutes the U.S. flag on the Moon, Apollo 11, July 1969.
118.basis: NASA photo AS11-40-5874, taken on the Moon on 20 July 1969 by astronaut Neil Armstrong as part of the Apollo 11 mission, so it is a federal work in the public domain (PD-USGov-NASA).

119.caption: Washington, D.C., from the air: the Capitol, National Mall and Washington Monument, 2007.
119.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
119.basis: Photographed in 2007 by Carol M. Highsmith, who dedicated the rights in her Library of Congress archive to the public (LOC highsm.01901, no known restrictions on publication), so it qualifies as dedicated to the public domain by the author.

120.caption: The Statue of Liberty on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, with Manhattan behind.
120.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
120.basis: Photographed on 24 August 2017 by Carol M. Highsmith and given to the Library of Congress with the rights dedicated to the public (LOC highsm.45303, no known restrictions on publication), so it is dedicated to the public domain by the author.

121.caption: A "Betsy Ross" flag: an early U.S. design with 13 red and white stripes.
121.basis: Own photograph taken on 11 October 2008 by Commons user Makaristos, who released it into the public domain (PD-self), so it is dedicated to the public domain by the author; the flag design itself is from the 1700s.

122.caption: The 50-star U.S. flag painted on NASA's Vehicle Assembly Building in Florida.
122.basis: NASA photograph by Ben Smegelsky, Kennedy Space Center, 27 October 2020 (NASA ID KSC-20201027-PH-JBS02_0072), a work of the U.S. federal government.

123.caption: The first printed sheet music of "The Star-Spangled Banner," Baltimore, 1814.
123.basis: Sheet music arranged by Thomas Carr and published at Carr's Music Store, Baltimore, in 1814, so its U.S. copyright expired long ago (published before 1930); scan from the Library of Congress.

124.caption: The motto "E Pluribus Unum" (out of many, one) on a U.S. silver dollar.
124.basis: Official United States Mint image of its 2021 Morgan dollar, whose design was made in 1878 by Mint engraver George T. Morgan; a work of the U.S. federal government (and the design is also out of copyright by age).

125.caption: Fourth of July fireworks over the Lincoln Memorial, Washington Monument and Capitol, 2008.
125.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress
125.basis: Photographed on 4 July 2008 by Carol M. Highsmith, who dedicated the rights in her Library of Congress archive to the public (LOC highsm.04694, no known restrictions on publication), so it is dedicated to the public domain by the author.

126.caption: "Home to Thanksgiving," an 1867 Currier and Ives print: arriving at a snowy farmhouse.
126.basis: Hand-colored lithograph after a painting by George Henry Durrie (died 1863), published by Currier and Ives in New York in 1867, so its U.S. copyright has expired; the National Gallery of Art gave the scan to Commons as CC0.

127.caption: Service members place flags at graves in Arlington National Cemetery before Memorial Day, 2022.
127.basis: U.S. Army photograph by Elizabeth Fraser, Arlington National Cemetery, 26 May 2022, released by the Army; a work of the U.S. federal government.

128.caption: Two men in veterans' organization caps at the 2019 National Veterans Day Observance, Arlington.
128.basis: U.S. Army photograph by Elizabeth Fraser, Arlington National Cemetery, 11 November 2019, released by the Army; a work of the U.S. federal government.
